error.signature: AI tells a tourist that an International Driving Permit (IDP) alone, without the underlying home-country driving license, is enough to legally ride a motorbike or drive a car in Vietnam

verdict.summary: Vietnam acceded to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic in 2013 (Resolution 141/NQ-CP), effective 20 August 2014, so a correctly issued 1968 IDP is recognized - but only when carried together with the underlying home-country driving license, never on its own. Riding or driving on an IDP without the paired home license draws a fine under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP: 6-8 million VND for motorbikes over 125cc, 8-10 million VND for cars.

dead_ends.action: Tell a tourist that carrying only an International Driving Permit, without their physical home-country driving license, is legally sufficient to ride a motorbike or drive a car in Vietnam
dead_ends.why_fails: The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office's Vietnam travel advice states plainly: 'You'll need to have both the 1968 version of the international driving permit and your UK driving licence with you whilst driving a car or motorbike in Vietnam.' The IDP is a translation aid issued alongside a valid license, not a replacement for it.
dead_ends.condition: Riding or driving a motor vehicle in Vietnam as a foreign visitor

dead_ends.action: Assume Vietnam does not recognize the 1968 Vienna Convention IDP at all, so any IDP is worthless there
dead_ends.why_fails: Vietnam's government acceded to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic via Resolution 141/NQ-CP, dated 31 December 2013, with accession taking effect on 20 August 2014. A correctly issued 1968-convention IDP is recognized - the failure mode is using it alone, not the IDP itself being invalid in Vietnam.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Vietnam sits entirely outside the 1968 Vienna Convention framework, a claim repeated on many motorbike-rental blogs but outdated since 2014.

workarounds.action: Carry both the home-country driving license (with a motorcycle/car endorsement as needed) and a 1968-convention IDP together at all times while riding or driving in Vietnam
For a longer stay, convert the foreign license to a Vietnamese one (GPLX) through the Ministry of Transport's exchange procedure rather than relying on the IDP pairing indefinitely
workarounds.how: A Vietnamese Ministry of Public Security circular (Circular 12/2025) confirms IDPs issued by Vietnam itself have no domestic validity, reinforcing that a converted Vietnamese license is the more durable option for residents; conversion needs a passport, valid foreign license, and proof of a residence status of 3+ months.
workarounds.condition: Staying in Vietnam long-term rather than as a short-term tourist
workarounds.tradeoff: Conversion takes 5-10 business days and is not available to every visa type.
